findings.detail: `currentBatchItems` is `uniqueItems.slice(...)`, and `uniqueItems` holds `{ text, context }` objects (built at TranslateTab.tsx:242), not strings. So `addLog(`Translated: "${currentBatchItems[idx]}" -> "${result}"`)` renders as `Translated: "[object Object]" -> "قميص أزرق"` for every successfully translated item. The expression predates this PR, but the block containing it was rewritten twice within this diff (the blank-result filter, then the `alignBatchResults` refactor) and carried forward unchanged. It matters here specifically because this PR's whole thesis is that the log is the record a user actually reads — and this is the one log line that fires on the happy path, so it is the majority of what they read. The exported workbook is unaffected, which is why this is medium rather than high.
findings.summary: Per-item success log prints "[object Object]" for the source text

findings.detail: `alignBatchResults` returns `usable` (the count of non-blank results), and four tests assert on it — but TranslateTab does not read it. Instead it recomputes exactly the same number as `batchTranslated` by incrementing inside the `forEach` at TranslateTab.tsx:315. The two derivations agree today by construction (both count trimmed non-empty strings), so this is not a bug; it is a second source of truth for the number that drives `processedUniqueCount`, the PARTIAL banner, and the filename prefix. If either definition of "counts as translated" is ever changed, only one side moves, and the divergence surfaces as a workbook whose banner disagrees with its own Status column — the class of silent-wrongness this util was extracted to prevent.
findings.summary: `usable` is computed and tested but never read in production

findings.detail: `IAiService.translateBatch` (types/ai.types.ts:18) and the free `translateBatch` (services/geminiService.ts:287) both gained `onNotice?`, but the class wrapper that implements the interface still declares `options: { sourceLang; targetLang; domain; glossary }`. Nothing breaks today: the wrapper forwards `options` wholesale, and TypeScript's method-parameter bivariance means the narrower type still satisfies `implements IAiService`, so `aiService.translateBatch(..., { onNotice })` in TranslateTab compiles and works. But the class is the seam `aiServiceFactory.ts` exists for ("simply replace GeminiService with the new implementation"), and it now advertises a contract that is one field short of the interface it implements. A caller holding the concrete `GeminiService` type and passing an object literal with `onNotice` would be rejected by the excess-property check for a property the function actually honours.
findings.summary: GeminiService.translateBatch's options type omits the new onNotice

findings.detail: The rewritten comment reads `# Google API (Gemini). No exemptions — see the note above.`, but the note explaining why `AIza…` carries no exemption starts at line 76, nine lines below. The text immediately above (lines 62-64) is about anchored provider prefixes, not exemptions — so a reader following the pointer lands on the wrong paragraph. Purely a navigation nit in a file that is otherwise scrupulous about explaining itself.
findings.summary: Comment points "above" at a note that is below it
